downside.story: P10: the Q4 FY2026 slowdown becomes the run-rate (room nights ~1% growth in FY2027 as the Middle East conflict and high airfares persist and Europe softens), AI-channel distribution (Google AI Mode booking, LLM agents) and hotel-direct pressure cut take rate 15 bp and lift marketing 15 bp of bookings, and the market prices BKNG like a structurally challenged intermediary (~11x NTM GAAP EPS, below EXPE's 15.3x).

base.story: Median: Q4 FY2026 dip to ~2.5% room nights, then ~5% in FY2027 and 4.5% in FY2028; bookings per night +2%; take rate eroding 5-8 bp a year on flight mix; marketing slightly up as a share of bookings; fixed costs +5%; GAAP EBIT margin ~34%; buybacks shrink the count 5.5% a year; 14.2x NTM EPS; $1.9B of litigation paid or expected.

upside.story: P90: the Q4 dip proves transitory (H1 2027 on-the-books 'healthy'), room nights return to ~7% growth, payments and Connected Trip hold the take rate, B2C marketing leverage resumes, AI referrals prove incremental, and the multiple recovers toward ~18x as the AI fear fades (still below the ~27x historical average cited by MarketScreener).

reasoning: Skeptic lane. Q3 FY2026 (10-Q/release 2026-11-03) beat its guide (room nights +6.7% vs 3-5%) but the CFO guided Q4 room nights to +1-3%, adjusted revenue +0-2% and adjusted EBITDA flat on investments, and cited end-of-quarter moderation and October disruptions (corrected transcript, Steenbergen). Reported revenue fell 1% because of a $900M FTC revenue reduction plus a $100M accrual for Priceline's B2B supply to deceptive third-party sites (Reuters/Techlicious; SF City Attorney suit), not yet paid. Litigation stack: EU hotel parity collective action (18,135 hotels, several billion euros, hearings 2027), Dutch consumer claims EUR 965M (jurisdiction upheld 2026-10-28), Spain EUR 413M fine under appeal. AI: Google moved agentic hotel booking into AI Mode in the US (Skift 2026-08-27) with Booking as a partner; LLM referrals are <1% of room nights (CFO). Sell-side mostly Buy but cutting (Wells Fargo EW $190; Feb 2026 cuts up to 23% on AI fears); Morgan Stanley sees AI as a channel and online travel +7% a year. Build: quarterly drivers (room nights, $/room night, take rate, marketing % bookings, fixed costs) calibrated to the supplements; FY2027 revenue $30,987M (-1.6% vs MarketScreener consensus $31,505M), EBIT $10,642M (-4.7% vs $11,162M), EPS ~$11.5 (-3% vs $11.85); NTM EPS at the horizon ~$12.2 vs consensus ~$13.5 (-10%: we have no share gains, continued take-rate dilution and +5% fixed costs). Valued at 14.2x (k-rule on a 2-peer median, less 0.75 turn AI risk) minus probability-weighted litigation. Downside/upside move the drivers and the multiple to genuine 1-in-10 cases; left tail fatter. Sources: 12 of 23 in lane; of the 16 non-company-filing/transcript sources, 12 (75%) are lane kinds (litigation, regulatory, critical press, target cuts, AI-threat trade press). Research limits: Nasdaq/Zacks consensus API not reachable (blocked), Twelve Data estimates need a higher plan; FY2027 consensus taken from MarketScreener.

downside.story: P10: the Q4 FY2026 slowdown becomes the run-rate (room nights ~1% growth in FY2027 as the Middle East conflict and high airfares persist and Europe softens), AI-channel distribution (Google AI Mode booking, LLM agents) and hotel-direct pressure cut take rate 15 bp and lift marketing 15 bp of bookings, and the market prices BKNG like a structurally challenged intermediary (~11x NTM GAAP EPS, below EXPE's 15.3x).

upside.story: P90: the Q4 dip proves transitory (H1 2027 on-the-books 'healthy'), room nights return to ~7% growth, payments and Connected Trip hold the take rate, B2C marketing leverage resumes, AI referrals prove incremental, and the multiple recovers toward ~18x as the AI fear fades (still below the ~27x historical average cited by MarketScreener).

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver set: revenue = room nights x gross bookings per room night x take rate; EBIT = revenue - (marketing % + 2.0% sales-and-other) x gross bookings - fixed operating costs (GAAP, after SBC). The value is carried by one P/E leg on the model's own NTM GAAP EPS at 2027-11-16 (Q4 FY2027-Q3 FY2028) at 14.2x, plus equity-level litigation adjustments (FTC accrual, Spain CNMC, EU hotel and Dutch consumer claims). No SOTP (advertising & other is ~4% of revenue, KAYAK written down), no DCF (policy). Driven share of revenue 100%. Drivers proposed by this forecaster; not yet card-approved by Kilian (rule 2).
model_inputs.gap_note: Judgment calls for Kilian: (1) exit P/E 14.2x rests on a 2-peer median (EXPE, ABNB); with EXPE alone as the median the k-rule gives 13.85x (-2.5% to target); with no AI deduction 14.96x (+5.4%) - card if the supervisor keeps it. (2) litigation adjustments ($-1,000M FTC at 100%, Spain 40%, EU hotels 30% of $1.68B, Dutch consumers 20% of $1.08B) total about -$1.9B or -$2.8/share (~-1.7%). (3) shareholder_returns FY2026 = $8,300M is NOT the FY2026 total (~$12.4B): the engine spreads a year's returns by quarterly revenue share and only the post-balance Q4 share (6,415/28,192 = 22.8% -> ~$1.9B) enters the cash roll from 2026-09-30. No financing event >=20% probability: buybacks are funded from FCF and the $12.4B authorization (src 1). Fair value matches the engine base (see fair_value).
